documents.title: Mack MP7 MP8 MP10 SPN 1231 FMI 9 inactive multiples-of-three workflow
documents.authority: OEM Mack Trucks technical solution archived by NHTSA
documents.summary: For Mack MP7, MP8 or MP10 powered trucks built from January 1, 2010 to January 1, 2013, an inactive SPN 1231 FMI 9 / U010E logged in multiples of three can be caused by an EECU-to-ACM communication timing issue. Mack's workflow says active faults should be troubleshot normally; if inactive and the counter is in multiples of three, update the EMS software. This is a narrow applicability rule and must not be generalized to active data-link faults or other model years.

documents.title: Meritor WABCO mBSP ABS ATC ESC TOOLBOX diagnostic workflow
documents.authority: OEM Meritor WABCO Maintenance Manual MM-1719
documents.summary: Meritor WABCO MM-1719 states that TOOLBOX software can display static and dynamic system information, active and stored faults with repair instructions, and activate components to verify operation and wiring. For applicable mBSP software, TOOLBOX 12.3 or higher is required. Adapter communication must be configured for the correct device and J1939 protocol. Diagnostic lesson: verify communication setup and use live/fault/component tests before replacing ABS/ESC hardware.

documents.title: Meritor WABCO ABS wheel-speed sensor maintenance check
documents.authority: OEM Meritor WABCO Maintenance Manual MM-1719
documents.summary: Meritor WABCO MM-1719 says wheel-speed-sensor adjustment should be checked and the sensor and sensor clip lubricated whenever wheel-end maintenance is performed, using recommended lubricant. The manual also advises checking the tractor ABS lamp at each vehicle start; it should illuminate momentarily. These are maintenance and initial inspection steps, not proof of a failed sensor or ECU.

documents.title: Caterpillar C15 2008-2009 ARD regeneration device safety campaign awareness
documents.authority: Caterpillar safety service letter / recall documentation archived by NHTSA
documents.summary: Caterpillar identified a safety issue on certain 2008-2009 C15 engines where the Aftertreatment Regeneration Device body could develop a hole and allow heat or flame to escape during DPF regeneration. The remedy included ARD body replacement and a software update for affected serial numbers. Panta must treat this as serial-number-specific safety campaign information: verify engine serial/campaign status rather than assuming every C15 regeneration complaint has this cause.
